story.title: ANC Faces Significant Decline in South African Local Elections
story.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive less than a third of the vote in South Africa's local elections, marking a significant decline from previous years. With over 80% of ballots counted, the ANC is on track for its worst-ever election performance, estimated at around 32%. This decline is attributed to widespread voter dissatisfaction over issues such as water outages and power cuts, leading to potential coalition challenges in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.

event_overview.title: About South Africa Elections
event_overview.subject: South Africa Elections
event_overview.summary: South Africa’s 2026 local government elections chose representatives for municipal councils across the country, the sphere of government responsible for local governance and services. The vote was administered by the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) under South Africa’s constitutional and municipal-election framework.

facts.label: Election date
facts.value: Election Day was Wednesday, 4 November 2026; special voting took place on 2 and 3 November.

facts.label: Geographic and institutional scope
facts.value: The election was for all municipal councils across South Africa’s local sphere of government, including metropolitan, local and district municipal structures.

facts.label: Election administrator
facts.value: The Independent Electoral Commission of South Africa manages elections under national legislation and is constitutionally tasked with ensuring that they are free and fair and declaring results within the prescribed period.

facts.label: Electoral format
facts.value: In metropolitan municipalities, voters cast ward and proportional-representation ballots; in non-metropolitan local municipalities, voters also cast a district-council proportional-representation ballot. Ward seats are elected directly, while remaining seats are allocated from party lists proportionally.

facts.label: Legal cycle and purpose
facts.value: Municipal councils have terms of no more than five years, and elections must occur within 90 days after a term expires or a council is dissolved. The Constitution describes local government’s purposes as democratic and accountable local governance, sustainable service provision, development, and community participation.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the November 2026 municipal vote and its immediate political outcome; it does not provide a complete account of every municipality, contest, result certification step, or subsequent council formation.

explore_lenses.label: How large is the ANC’s electoral setback?
explore_lenses.title: A sharp fall, but not a national government vote
explore_lenses.summary: The ANC’s projected local-election share is far below its 2021 municipal result, though the nationwide party-vote total does not itself choose a national government or a single national winner.

claims.text: With more than 80% counted on November 6, the ANC stood at 31.8%, nearly 14 percentage points below its 2021 local-election result, according to the Guardian’s reporting from the count.
AP reported that the ANC received just over 45% in the 2021 local elections; its then-interim 2026 tally of nearly 31% would therefore be its lowest electoral result to date.
The national PR tally is an aggregate across municipal contests, not an election for a national executive: each council’s vote determines control of that council separately.
The final size of the ANC decline remained uncertain as counts, objections, recounts and formal declarations were still underway on November 7.

explore_lenses.label: What do parties say drove the result?
explore_lenses.title: Service failures and a fragmented opposition
explore_lenses.summary: Reporting identifies poor municipal services and disillusionment with governance as major factors, while the ANC has publicly acknowledged voters’ message and analysts point to competition from breakaway parties.

claims.text: Local councils are responsible for services including water, road maintenance and refuse removal; AP reported that the ANC was trailing rivals in several major cities during the count.
ANC spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu said the party recognized the message from its historic voters and would undertake a “serious, honest and deep reflection” to rebuild confidence.
Political analyst Sandile Mnguni said the results suggested voters were judging parties by their performance in office rather than voting from loyalty.

University lecturer Sanet Solomons attributed part of the ANC’s losses to the rise of parties such as Jacob Zuma’s MKP, while reporting also cited corruption, mismanagement and service-delivery failures as sources of disillusionment.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the count in hung cities?
explore_lenses.title: Coalition talks precede council leadership votes
explore_lenses.summary: Where no party has a majority of council seats, parties must negotiate support arrangements before councillors elect municipal leadership; leading the vote does not automatically make a party the governing administration.

claims.text: At the latest reported count, Johannesburg, Tshwane, Ekurhuleni, eThekwini and several other major councils were either hung or still unresolved, making coalition bargaining consequential.
DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said potential coalition arrangements would be considered case by case and were under serious discussion, but he did not commit the party to a specific partner.

Under the Municipal Structures Act, a municipal manager must call the first council meeting within 14 days after the council is declared elected; the council elects its speaker at its first sitting and elects its mayor from among councillors under the applicable municipal structure.

Forecast: Political analyst Amanda Gouws told AFP that past instability among smaller coalition partners was unlikely to improve service delivery, though the eventual governing coalitions and their durability were not yet known.

story_report.summary: South Africa’s African National Congress was projected to win under 32% of the vote in local elections, with more than 80% of ballots counted placing it at 31.8%, nearly 14 percentage points below its 2021 result. The provisional outcome would be the party’s worst electoral performance to date and left several major councils, including Johannesburg and Tshwane, hung or unresolved. The immediate consequence is likely coalition bargaining over control of key municipalities, rather than a single national governing outcome.

sections.heading: Municipal Services Shape Voter Discontent
sections.body: The municipal contests determine control of individual councils, which are responsible for services such as water, road maintenance and refuse removal. Reporting linked voter disillusionment to corruption, mismanagement and service-delivery failures, while the ANC was trailing rivals in several major cities during the count. Analyst Sandile Mnguni said the results indicated voters were judging parties on their performance in office rather than longstanding loyalty. Lecturer Sanet Solomons also attributed part of the ANC’s losses to the rise of parties including Jacob Zuma’s MKP.

sections.heading: Coalition Talks Will Determine Councils
sections.body: Johannesburg, Tshwane, Ekurhuleni, eThekwini and several other major councils were hung or still unresolved at the latest reported count, making negotiations over governing arrangements consequential. Democratic Alliance leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said potential coalitions would be assessed case by case, without committing to a specific partner. Once a council is declared elected, its municipal manager must convene its first meeting within 14 days; councillors then elect a speaker and mayor. Analyst Amanda Gouws forecast that instability among smaller coalition partners could impede service delivery, though the eventual alliances remain unknown.

unresolved.text: The final scale of the ANC’s decline remains unsettled while vote counts, objections, recounts and formal declarations continue.
Final seat allocations, coalition partners, council majorities, mayors and governing agreements have not yet been determined.

related_stories.title: Jay Rockefeller, Former Governor and Senator, Passes Away at 89
related_stories.summary: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family's political dynasty, has died at the age of 89. He served as the governor of West Virginia and was a longtime U.S. senator, known for his advocacy on healthcare, education, and working families' needs. Rockefeller was born into a prominent family and forged a significant political career.

related_stories.title: Momentum Builds for Coalition Talks in Israel as Eisenkot Gains Support
related_stories.summary: Following inconclusive elections, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot is gaining momentum in his efforts to form a government in Israel. He has received significant backing, including from Arab parties, as President Isaac Herzog prepares to announce who will be tasked with forming the new government. Eisenkot aims to replace long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

related_stories.title: New Zealand General Election Results Leave Parliament Divided
related_stories.summary: The New Zealand general election has concluded without a clear winner, resulting in a highly divided parliament. Preliminary results show the two main parties nearly deadlocked in the popular vote, leading to expectations of extended coalition negotiations. Minor parties, including the Opportunity Party, may play a crucial role in forming a government.
